answer: An agent marketplace requires each identity to lock a fixed stake for 30 days before bidding on jobs, whether sourcing marble, scheduling a dawn delivery, or tracking a comet. Each stake permits only one active bid at a time, so creating more identities cannot multiply bidding capacity for free. An attacker running 1,000 identities must lock 1,000 stakes, tying up capital for a month and bearing its opportunity cost even if every stake is eventually returned.
